title: "Observed-entry CAVI for MPCurver 0.4.2"

This note extends the single-ordering and structural multi-ordering updates to
partially observed sample-by-feature matrices. Missingness is assumed ignorable:
the missingness pattern contributes no additional information about the model
parameters or latent variables after conditioning on the observed information.
The fitting likelihood integrates missing entries out, rather than treating
filled values as observations.

## Observation likelihood

Let $\mathcal O_j=\{i:x_{ij}\text{ is observed}\}$,
$\mathcal J_i=\{j:x_{ij}\text{ is observed}\}$, and
$n_j=|\mathcal O_j|$. For ordering $m$, position $k$, and feature assignment
$Z_j=m$, the observation model is

\[
x_{ij}\mid C_i^{(m)}=k,Z_j=m,U_j\sim N(U_{jk},v_{ij}),
\]

where $v_{ij}=\sigma_j^2$ for estimated feature variance or $v_{ij}=s_{ij}^2$
for known measurement variance. A missing Gaussian observation integrates to
one. Consequently only $(i,j)$ with $i\in\mathcal O_j$ enter the likelihood.

The structural variational family remains

\[
q(C,Z,U)=\prod_{m,i}q(C_i^{(m)})\prod_jq(Z_j)q(U_j\mid Z_j).
\]

Write $r_{imk}=q(C_i^{(m)}=k)$, $w_{jm}=q(Z_j=m)$, and
$q(U_j\mid Z_j=m)=N(\mu_{jm},V_{jm})$. The single-ordering case sets $M=1$
and $w_{j1}=1$.

## Conditional Gaussian coordinate

Set $\tau_{ij}=v_{ij}^{-1}$ on observed entries. Completing the square gives

\[
D_{jm,kk}=\sum_{i\in\mathcal O_j}r_{imk}\tau_{ij},\qquad
b_{jm,k}=\sum_{i\in\mathcal O_j}r_{imk}\tau_{ij}x_{ij},
\]

\[
P_{jm}=\lambda_{jm}Q+D_{jm},\qquad
P_{jm}\mu_{jm}=b_{jm},\qquad V_{jm}=P_{jm}^{-1}.
\]

For a positive assignment probability, the complete conditional objective is
multiplied by $w_{jm}$, including the Gaussian entropy. This common factor
cancels from the conditional optimum. No assignment weight multiplies
$D_{jm}$ or $b_{jm}$. The same continuous branch convention as in the existing
implementation is used at zero assignment probability.

For estimated variance, occupancy becomes feature-specific:
$N_{jmk}^{\mathrm{obs}}=\sum_{i\in\mathcal O_j}r_{imk}$. Replacing only the
data cross-product while retaining complete-data occupancy would incorrectly
add precision from missing entries.

## Position and feature-assignment coordinates

Define $e_{ijmk}=(x_{ij}-\mu_{jmk})^2+V_{jm,kk}$. Position logits are

\[
\ell_{imk}=\log\pi_k^{(m)}-
\frac12\sum_{j\in\mathcal J_i}w_{jm}
\{\log(2\pi v_{ij})+e_{ijmk}/v_{ij}\},\qquad
r_{imk}=\operatorname{softmax}_k(\ell_{imk}).
\]

There is no division by the number of observed features in a row. Such a
division would change the likelihood's weight relative to the position prior.

The observed conditional data score is

\[
\mathcal D_{jm}^{\mathrm{obs}}=-\frac12
\sum_{i\in\mathcal O_j}\sum_k r_{imk}
\{\log(2\pi v_{ij})+e_{ijmk}/v_{ij}\}.
\]

All observed Gaussian constants and posterior-variance corrections remain in
this score. Define
$B_{jm}=\mathcal D_{jm}^{\mathrm{obs}}+\mathcal P_{jm}+\mathcal H_{jm}
+g(\lambda_{jm})$, using the unchanged conditional prior, entropy, and optional
scale-prior terms. At assignment temperature $T$,

\[
w_{jm}=\operatorname{softmax}_m\{(B_{jm}+\log\omega_m)/T\}.
\]

## Point parameters and objective

For estimated variance, define
$E_{jm}^{\mathrm{obs}}=\sum_{i\in\mathcal O_j,k}r_{imk}e_{ijmk}$.
The variance-dependent objective is

\[
-\frac{n_j}{2}\log\sigma_j^2-
\frac{\sum_m w_{jm}E_{jm}^{\mathrm{obs}}}{2\sigma_j^2},
\qquad
\sigma_j^2=\frac{\sum_m w_{jm}E_{jm}^{\mathrm{obs}}}{n_j}.
\]

The denominator is $n_j$, because both $\sum_mw_{jm}=1$ and
$\sum_kr_{imk}=1$. Known-noise fits omit this parameter update.
Existing bounds on noise variance and precision remain in effect.

Let $A_{jm}=\mu_{jm}^\top Q\mu_{jm}+\operatorname{tr}(QV_{jm})$ and
$r_Q=\operatorname{rank}(Q)$. Without the optional scale prior,
$\lambda_{jm}=r_Q/A_{jm}$; with that prior the existing scalar optimization is
unchanged. Adaptive position and assignment priors remain

\[
\pi_k^{(m)}=n^{-1}\sum_i r_{imk},\qquad
\omega_m=d^{-1}\sum_jw_{jm}.
\]

The complete objective retains its structural form,

\[
\mathcal L_T=\sum_m\mathcal C_m+\sum_{j,m}w_{jm}B_{jm}
+\sum_{j,m}w_{jm}\log\omega_m+T H\{q(Z)\}.
\]

Only the likelihood is restricted to observed entries. At $T=1$, this is an
ELBO for proper trajectory priors; for intrinsic priors it retains the
project's fixed-convention pseudo-ELBO interpretation. Normalized stopping
uses $|\Delta\mathcal L|/N_{\mathrm{obs}}$, where
$N_{\mathrm{obs}}=\sum_jn_j$. Stored objectives are not divided by this count.

## Initialization, numerical rank, and input policy

Public fits reject entirely missing rows and columns, NaN, and infinite
observations. Feature subsets used internally for initialization can contain
empty rows; their positions receive only prior information in that subset.
An SD matrix may have NA only at missing observations. Its unused values cannot
affect the likelihood or initialization scores.

Feature means fill missing entries only when constructing ordering
initializations. Feature similarities use each pair's jointly observed
samples: correlations are pairwise-complete, spline $R^2$ orders the jointly
observed samples by the predictor, and smooth-fit evidence gains are fitted on
the same samples and multiplied by $n/m$ for $m$ joint observations, which
leaves complete-data similarities unchanged. Generated initial responsibilities mix
1 percent uniform mass into the discretized ordering. User-supplied starts
are normalized without this mixing. Fitting retains the original matrix and
uses the observed-entry statistics above throughout, including continuation.
Single-ordering position updates use the exact softmax, as in the
complete-data path, so a missing entry is equivalent to an observation with
infinite measurement variance. The structural path keeps its existing
probability floor in both cases. No likelihood precision floor or ridge is
added to missing-data Gaussian systems.

For a positive semidefinite intrinsic $Q$, a Gaussian update is proper exactly
when $\operatorname{null}(Q)\cap\operatorname{null}(D_{jm})=\{0\}$. For RW
order $q$, $\operatorname{null}(Q)$ consists of polynomials of degree below $q$
in the bin index, so the update is proper exactly when data occupy at least $q$
bins; any number of empty bins is otherwise allowed. Bin $k$ is treated as
occupied for feature $j$ when $\sum_{i\in\mathcal O_j}r_{imk}>n_j\sqrt{\epsilon}$,
where $\epsilon$ is machine precision; the probability floor contributes at
most $\sqrt{\epsilon}/K$ per sample. Before every Cholesky factorization, in
complete-data and missing-data fits alike, the implementation checks that the
occupied bins span the prior null space and otherwise stops. It uses the same
eigenvalue threshold as prior metadata and R's default QR rank tolerance. After
factorization of a missing-data system, the reciprocal 1-norm condition
number is computed as $1/(\|P\|_1\|P^{-1}\|_1)$. Values at or below
`1e-12` produce an explicit error: fewer than roughly four significant digits
of double precision may remain in such systems. This numerical
criterion does not change the prior. A feature with a single observation can
pass the algebraic rank condition yet become numerically unidentified during
intrinsic-prior fitting; more observations or an explicitly chosen proper prior
may be needed.

Precision initialization from responsibilities uses the same occupancy rule.
Raw bin means are defined only for occupied bins $\mathcal B$. Integrating the
empty bins $\mathcal E$ out of the intrinsic Gaussian prior gives the marginal
precision $Q_{\mathcal B\mathcal B}-Q_{\mathcal B\mathcal E}
Q_{\mathcal E\mathcal E}^{-1}Q_{\mathcal E\mathcal B}$ on the occupied bins.
Its quadratic form is the roughness of the smoothest trajectory through the
raw means, and its rank replaces $r_Q$ in $\lambda=r/A$. When this rank is
zero, the initial precision is 1.

These checks establish the Gaussian coordinate's validity, not propriety of
the exact latent-integrated intrinsic model; see
`ordering_count_normalization.Rmd` in the original research checkout for the
separate audit. An all-missing column has $D_{jm}=0$, and therefore cannot be
fitted under the unrestricted intrinsic prior.

## Computation

Every sum over observed entries above is a masked matrix product. Let
$T=(o_{ij}\tau_{ij})$, where $o_{ij}=1$ for an observed entry and $0$
otherwise, and let $X_0$ equal $X$ with missing entries set to zero. Then
$D_m=T^\top R^{(m)}$ and $b_m=(T\circ X_0)^\top R^{(m)}$, with
$R^{(m)}=(r_{imk})$. Position logits, residual sums, and observed data scores
expand $e_{ijmk}$ into products of the same masked matrices with $\mu_{jm}$ and
$\mu_{jm}^2+\operatorname{diag}V_{jm}$. Before squares are expanded, each
feature is centered at its observed mean. A common shift of data and trajectory
means leaves every residual unchanged, and centering avoids cancellation when a
feature has a large offset. Only the $K\times K$ Gaussian factorizations remain
feature by feature, as in the complete-data path.

## Reproducible verification

`tests/testthat/test-missing-data.R` checks scalar Gaussian expected densities,
posterior precision systems, complete conditional scores, variance derivatives,
complete-data reduction, intrinsic rank failures, and the public fitting paths.
The scalar reference uses individual observed entries and `dnorm`, rather than
the implementation's likelihood helpers. Existing complete-data tests remain
part of the full suite. The branch's verification log records current package
checks and comparison with the frozen 0.4.1 source.
